locator: §7, "Quine rejected Carnap’s internal/external distinction, which in Quine’s view relied on an analytic/synthetic distinction"
interpretation: The entry's report of Quine's objection. The same section reports that the now mainstream reading (Creath) holds that Quine partly misunderstood Carnap, and that whether the internal/external distinction needs the analytic/synthetic distinction is itself an open topic (Thomasson). Attribution reading on a secondary witness.
attribution: The passage states that Quine rejected Carnap's internal/external distinction because in his view it relied on an analytic/synthetic distinction, accepting a framework consisting in accepting the sentences analytic in it, which is the premise.
